From 29ab768277617452d88c0607c9299cdc63b6e9ff Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 11:27:20 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] PM: runtime: Fix a race condition related to device removal

The following code in pm_runtime_work() may dereference the dev->parent
pointer after the parent device has been freed:

	/* Maybe the parent is now able to suspend. */
	if (parent && !parent->power.ignore_children) {
		spin_unlock(&dev->power.lock);

		spin_lock(&parent->power.lock);
		rpm_idle(parent, RPM_ASYNC);
		spin_unlock(&parent->power.lock);

		spin_lock(&dev->power.lock);
	}

Fix this by inserting a flush_work() call in pm_runtime_remove().

Without this patch blktest block/001 triggers the following complaint
sporadically:

diff --git a/drivers/base/power/runtime.c b/drivers/base/power/runtime.c
index 0ee8ea971aa4..335288e8b5b3 100644
--- a/drivers/base/power/runtime.c
+++ b/drivers/base/power/runtime.c
@@ -1895,6 +1895,7 @@ void pm_runtime_reinit(struct device *dev)
 void pm_runtime_remove(struct device *dev)
 {
 	__pm_runtime_disable(dev, false);
+	flush_work(&dev->power.work);
 	pm_runtime_reinit(dev);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

**`drivers/base/power/runtime.c`**  
- In the function `pm_runtime_remove()`, a call to `flush_work(&dev->power.work)` was inserted **before** the `pm_runtime_reinit(dev)` call.  
- This ensures that any pending runtime PM work item (i.e., `pm_runtime_work()`) for the device is fully completed before the device’s runtime PM state is reinitialized.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The **single change** is a preventive synchronization step: it addresses a race condition where `pm_runtime_work()` could access `dev->parent` after the parent device had been freed during removal.  
- By flushing the workqueue entry, the patch guarantees that no concurrent runtime PM work is still running or queued when `pm_runtime_remove()` proceeds to reinitialize the device. This eliminates the possibility of a use-after-free access from `pm_runtime_work()` to the parent pointer.  
- The fix is minimal and self-contained, affecting only the removal path without altering other parts of the runtime PM framework.
